name: Berlin Arrives at the Harbor
description: Berlin's Mercedes drives down the coast road, moving steadily toward the harbor. The car descends the winding path beside the sand dunes, approaching the edge of the lagoon where the small harbor lies.
related_events: Mercedes descends coast road toward harbor

name: BERLIN Arrives at the Institute
description: A high wind sweeps through the chimneys, rustling the air above the institute. From this height, the figure of BERLIN emerges from a parked vehicle, stretching briefly before beginning to walk toward the building. The distance makes him appear small, a solitary shape moving across the open space below, visible under the wide sky.
related_events: BERLIN parks vehicle and exits
BERLIN walks toward the institute

name: Arrival at the Mansion
description: The Chevrolet turns in and parks in front of the mansion. The passengers step out, their breath visible in the cold air. They glance around at the snow-covered pines, the slush on the ground, the rows of parked cars, and the imposing structure before them. Without speaking, they close the car doors and begin walking toward the entrance.
related_events: Chevrolet arrives and parks in front of mansion
Passengers exit vehicle and approach mansion entrance

name: Berlin Wakes on a Mattress in an Abandoned House
description: Berlin opened his eyes on a new mattress wrapped in polythene, lying in the middle of an empty room. Bare wooden boards stretched in every direction. Sunlight filtered through dusty windows. A stone fireplace stood against one wall, cold and unused. A narrow set of stairs led upward to a small room above. Birds sang outside. He sat up slowly, looking around, taking in the peeling walls and broken floorboards. The place was empty except for the mattress. He ran a hand over the plastic covering, then glanced at the ceiling, listening to the silence.
related_events: Berlin awakens on a new mattress in an abandoned house

name: Ross Drives Toward the Isolated Building
description: Ross's car bursts into view, speeding along the valley road. Sunlight glints off fresh snow as the vehicle follows the curve of the landscape, heading toward a distant Victorian-style building. The structure looms with a clock tower and rows of dark, lifeless windows. The car vanishes around a bend, moving steadily closer to the somber architecture.
related_events: Ross's car enters the frame and speeds along the valley road
Car approaches isolated Victorian-style building with clock tower

name: Berlin Navigates Intersection and Discards Cigarette
description: Berlin sits alone in the car, surrounded by cigarette smoke. As an intersection approaches, he turns on the indicator and shifts lanes. He rolls down the window, takes a final drag from his cigarette, and flicks the butt out into the air.
related_events: Berlin signals and changes lanes before intersection
Berlin winds down car window
Berlin exits cigarette butt from car window

name: Ross and Berlin Find a Severed Hand in a Trash Sack
description: Ross crouches in the garbage, shining a flashlight into a torn trash sack. He peers inside and says, 'You're right. It's a fucken hand.' He passes the flashlight to Berlin, who takes a closer look at the severed hand inside the sack. After examining it, Berlin stands up, turns off the flashlight, and hands it back to Ross. 'I think you're here all day,' he says.
related_events: Ross discovers a severed hand in a trash sack
Berlin examines the severed hand in the trash sack
Berlin turns off the flashlight and returns it to Ross
Berlin tells Ross he will be at the scene all day

name: Berlin Arrives at the Institute and Talks with Helena
description: Berlin drives up the driveway lined with tall pines and parks the car, setting the handbrake with a sharp click. He steps out, joining Helena near the vehicle. As they stand together, he speaks about leaving Los Angeles, saying he couldn't take another day of it, how it felt like he'd spent his life apologizing in every street. He tells her about becoming a Scientific Services Officer, then getting transferred to the institute. The conversation winds down as he turns to her and says he's going to buy her a cup of coffee.
related_events: Berlin arrives at the institute and parks the car
Berlin recounts career change due to burnout
Berlin offers to buy Helena a cup of coffee

name: Berlin Arrives at Mrs. Citrine's House
description: Berlin pulls up to a pretty little house on a sunlit street with hills in the distance. He steps out of his Mercedes, adjusts his tie, and walks up the path. He reaches the door and presses the chimes. The door opens, revealing Mrs. Citrine, who offers a polite smile. She lets him in, and he steps inside.
related_events: Berlin arrives at Citrine's house and adjusts his tie
Berlin rings the door chimes at Citrine's house
Berlin enters Citrine's house after being welcomed

name: Chevrolet Passes Roadblock at Dump Entrance
description: A Chevrolet winds its way up a shabby canyon road leading to the city dump. At the final bend, a line of garbage trucks sits stalled, engines roaring, unable to move forward. Ahead, a Sheriff's car blocks the entrance. A uniformed officer steps out and waves the Chevrolet through the blockade. The car continues on, passing the stopped trucks and the officer, and moves toward the dump.
related_events: Chevrolet navigates winding road toward city dump
Garbage trucks queue at final road bend
Sheriff's car blocks access to dump entrance
Uniformed officer signals Chevrolet to proceed

name: Berlin and Ross Follow Voice Directions to Reception
description: Berlin and Ross arrive at the main entrance of a building. A recorded voice announces, 'YOU ARE NOW AT THE MAIN ENTRANCE. THERE ARE SIX STEPS.' They begin to climb the steps, and midway up, the voice adds, 'RECEPTION IS THROUGH SWING DOORS AND TO YOUR RIGHT.' As they ascend, Ross turns to look back.
related_events: Ross and Berlin arrive at main entrance of building
Recorded voice announces presence at main entrance
Recorded voice provides directions to reception
Ross looks back while ascending steps

name: BERLIN Checks the Gas Supply After the Cooker Fails
description: The gas flame on the cooker sputtered and went out as BERLIN stood nearby, preparing coffee. He reached for the knob, turning and clicking it several times, but the flame did not return. Kneeling, he lifted the edge of the cooker and peered beneath, then moved to the back door, crouching to follow a rubber gas pipe that ran underneath. He traced its length, examining the connection in the dim light.
related_events: Gas flame on cooker extinguishes unexpectedly
BERLIN attempts to relight the gas cooker
BERLIN inspects rubber gas supply pipe under back door

name: Berlin Searches for Usable Kitchen Items
description: Berlin opens the kitchen cupboards, moving aside old and chipped dishes. He pulls out a single cup, examines it briefly, and sets it down. The kitchen is outdated—a large china sink, a bulky refrigerator, and a working cooker. A dented kettle sits on the gas stove. He checks the cupboards again, then stops. His lips form a silent word as the flame beneath the kettle goes out. He crouches, then drops to his hands and knees, reaching under the back door to inspect a rubber pipe running along the floor.
related_events: BERLIN searches kitchen cupboards for usable items

name: Citrine Receives the Teletype Report on Jennifer
description: Citrine stands by the teletype machine, watching as the transmission about Jennifer slowly prints out. The paper emerges with fragmented details—approximate date of birth, approximate date of death, identity unknown. He pulls the page free and reads it, his expression tightening with unease. Nearby, a chair rests upside down on a desk. Ross remains at his post, sifting through documents with Detective Serato, the air thick with cigarette smoke and the quiet rustle of papers. As Citrine moves away from the machine, Ross looks up and calls out, 'Chief, I gotta talk to ya about this fat lady?' Citrine glances over. 'What about her?' 'She's making my life a misery... I wanna give her a lie-detector test.' Citrine continues down the room, saying, 'Alright, we'll talk about it.'
related_events: Citrine waits for teletype transmission about Jennifer
Citrine retrieves and reads teletype output with visible hesitation

name: Ross Asks for a Lie-Detector Test
description: Citrine walks past, heading up the carpet, as Ross calls out to him. Ross, standing near his desk with a detective named Serato, looks up from the documents he’s been going through. He tells Citrine he needs to talk about a woman he calls 'this fat lady' who’s been making his life difficult. He asks for permission to give her a lie-detector test. Citrine doesn’t stop but says they’ll talk about it, and keeps walking.
related_events: Ross interrupts Citrine to request a lie-detector test for a woman
Citrine agrees to discuss Ross's request

name: Arrive at Station and Enter During Downpour
description: The Mercedes rolled down the incline and came to a stop. Berlin stepped out into the rain and opened the trunk, pulling out an aquarium and an insulated picnic box. Blattis stood nearby, holding out a large yellow umbrella and offering to help carry the equipment. Water streamed heavily from the sky, cold and sharp. As they moved across the lot, Blattis remarked that the rain averaged 48 inches a year, falling without letup from October to June. He added that summers were better, with a crude comment about tourists. Reaching the station door, he punched in a security code, the keypad glowing faintly under wet fingers, then pushed the door open. They stepped inside, leaving the downpour behind.
related_events: Berlin exits Mercedes and unloads equipment from trunk
Blattis offers umbrella and assistance with equipment
Blattis comments on local rainfall patterns
Blattis makes crude remark about summer tourism
Blattis enters security code to access station
related_occasions: Arrival And Entry At Police Station During Heavy Rain

name: Ross and Berlin Arrive at the Staff Entrance
description: Ross and Berlin stand in a long, empty corridor. Yellow paint streaks the walls, fading in patches. Ross looks around, uneasy, and mutters that he hates the place, especially the silence. Berlin shrugs, suggesting they’re on the staff side of the building. A distant sound, like children singing, drifts from far away. Berlin reaches out and rings a doorbell. After a moment, footsteps approach. The door opens to reveal Helena Robertson, a young woman in her early twenties, blonde, with delicate features and dark eyes. She keeps her gaze averted as they exchange brief introductions. Ross and Berlin step inside, glancing at each other as they realize she is blind.
related_events: Ross and Berlin arrive at the staff side of the building
Helena Robertson opens the door to Ross and Berlin

name: Ross and Berlin Realize Helena Is Blind
description: Helena Robertson opens the door, her delicate features and dark eyes briefly meeting the visitors before she looks away, as if shy. Ross and Berlin step inside, exchanging glances as they follow her in. They notice she does not make eye contact, her gaze remaining unfocused. A moment passes before they both realize she is blind.
related_events: Ross and Berlin realize Helena is blind

name: Helena and Berlin Climb Stairs During Storm
description: A storm rages outside as Helena and Berlin make their way up the dimly lit stairwell. The elevator sits idle on one of the floors, its doors half open, but they continue on foot. Wind howls through the building, echoing in the narrow space. As they climb, Helena describes the sound of a car she heard—'hollow,' she says, unlike the 'fat' sound of local vehicles. Berlin presses her on the detail, skeptical, asking if it might have been a foreign car. They round a corner on the stairs, their voices rising over the storm. Each step is heavy, breath visible in the cold air. Three more flights remain.
related_events: Helena and Berlin converse while ascending stairs during a storm
Helena and Berlin continue ascending stairs despite elevator availability

name: Passing the Broken Elevator
description: The elevator stands on their floor with its doors half open, motionless. Berlin remarks that it breaks down all the time. He says they keep threatening to replace it, but they never will. Without stopping, they continue up the stairs.
related_events: Berlin comments on frequent elevator breakdowns

name: Ross Fixes the Boat Engine
description: Ross, his hands slick with oil, wrestles with the sputtering engine of his 35-foot fisherman. The brass and varnish of the boat gleam despite its age, much like Ross himself. He glances over and waves at his son Bobby, calling out, "Watch those revs there." Then, turning to Berlin, he says, "Would you shut it down a minute, Ross? This is important." Ross signals Bobby, who reaches over and cuts the engine. The diesel coughs and falls silent. "Alright, let's take a walk around the block," Ross says. "I gotta buy a gasket."
related_events: Ross struggles with malfunctioning boat engine
Ross signals Bobby to turn off the boat engine
Ross decides to take a walk around the block

name: Berlin Shares Ballistics Dead End and New Leads
description: The engine of Ross's boat roars as he works, his hands covered in oil. Berlin raises his voice to be heard over the noise, telling Ross that the slug pulled from the crime scene is made of soft lead and won't yield a ballistics match. He says he’s already called a contact in Los Angeles who ran a search through a mainframe for similar cases involving twenty-two caliber shootings. The search turned up something in San Diego. Ross briefly looks away to shout a warning to his son, Bobby, about the engine revs. Berlin asks him to shut the engine down so they can talk. Bobby cuts the engine, and the noise subsides. Ross says they should take a walk—he needs to buy a gasket.
related_events: Berlin reports ballistics analysis results
Berlin initiates search for similar shooting cases

name: Berlin and Ann Make Calls
description: Berlin sits at a desk with a legal pad covered in names and numbers, speaking on the phone. He asks how old the person is and writes down '26.' He listens, then asks how long ago the person was last seen—about six weeks. He looks hopefully toward Ann, who is on another call at the same desk. Ann approaches and places a sheet of notes in front of him. Berlin ends his call and dials a new number. Ann returns to her seat and continues her own conversation. Berlin speaks into the phone: 'Hello... Yes, this is Sergeant Berlin... My assistant explained?... How long ago was that?' He listens, nods, and asks for the name. 'Goodridge? O.K., I'll hold.'
related_events: Berlin and Ann conduct simultaneous phone inquiries from a shared workspace
Berlin asks about the age of the potential candidate during a phone call
Berlin learns the candidate named Lesley is a boy
Berlin expresses disappointment upon realizing the candidate does not meet his criteria

name: Berlin Takes New Call While Ross Brings News
description: Ann approaches Berlin's desk and places a sheet of notes in front of him, signaling a new lead. Berlin immediately ends his current phone call and dials the Shasta-Trinity Institute. He identifies himself as Sergeant Berlin and begins gathering information about a missing person—a 22-year-old woman with dark hair, studying mathematics, last seen five weeks ago. As he listens and takes notes, Ross enters the room, smiling, and announces, "Pig Woman agreed to take a test."
related_events: Ann delivers a sheet of notes to Berlin's desk and alerts him to a new call
Berlin initiates a phone call with Shasta-Trinity Institute

Ross enters the room with positive news about Pig Woman

name: Find the Empty Gas Cylinder
description: He enters the garage and sees the gas cylinder lying there. It is empty. He drags his fingers through his hair, then looks around at the clutter filling the space. Beyond, clouds gather on the horizon, and the fields stretch out, ready for rain. His neighbor is about 200 yards away, a cow fifty. The house sits remote, with a veranda at the back. He turns away as a dreary female voice begins to speak.
related_events: Character discovers empty gas cylinder in garage
Character expresses frustration by running hands through hair

name: Survey the Garage and the Gathering Storm
description: He drags his fingers through his hair, then looks around the garage at the heaps of clutter. His gaze shifts outside, taking in the clouds building on the horizon, the fields heavy with the threat of rain. His nearest neighbor is about 200 yards away, a cow some 50 yards off. The house sits remote and still, with a veranda at the back. He turns away as a dreary female voice begins to speak.
related_events: Character surveys cluttered surroundings in garage
Character observes approaching storm clouds and rural landscape

name: Walking Away as a Voice Emerges
description: He turns and walks away from the garage, hands at his sides, shoulders slightly hunched. As he moves across the uneven ground, a dreary female voice begins to drift through the air, tone flat and uninvited, filling the space behind him.
related_events: Dreary female voice intrudes as character walks away

name: Berlin Digs Up the Dog's Remains
description: In the cold winter mist, Berlin digs through the frozen ground with a shovel, sweat on his brow despite the chill. Trimble stands nearby, holding a flashlight to illuminate the graves. One after another, the pits open up in the earth. When Berlin reaches the twelfth grave, he stops suddenly. 'Get that lamp down here,' he says. The beam shifts, revealing white lime and clumps of black fur. Berlin crouches, shining a small flashlight into the hole. He gestures for Trimble to bring over a bag. Trimble flicks open a switchblade and hands Berlin a knife and a pair of long-nosed pliers. With the light clenched in his teeth, Berlin works carefully, then pulls a crumpled bullet from the back of the Labrador’s skull. He holds it up. 'Looks like a 22?' Trimble shakes his head. 'Me... I love dogs. Ask him?'
related_events: Berlin digs graves in winter mist
Berlin discovers the Dog's remains

name: Berlin Examines the Dog's Body
description: Gloom thickens around the flashlights as a winter mist falls. Trimble and Doberman watch silently while Berlin works over the dog's remains, a small flashlight clenched between his teeth. He gestures toward a bag and tells Trimble to get a knife and a pair of long-nosed pliers. Trimble retrieves the tools, flicking open the switchblade with a snap. Berlin cuts into the remains, probing carefully. After a moment, he pulls a crumpled bullet from the back of the Labrador's skull. He holds it up under the light—small caliber, badly deformed. 'Looks like a 22?' Trimble asks. Berlin turns to him, flashlight still in his mouth, and mumbles, 'You didn't shoot him, did you?' Trimble replies, 'Me? I love dogs. Ask him?'
related_events: Trimble retrieves a knife and pliers from a bag
Berlin retrieves a bullet from the Labrador's skull

name: Berlin Questions Trimble About the Dog's Shooting
description: Berlin holds up the crumpled bullet removed from the back of the Labrador's skull, examining it in the dim light. 'Looks like a 22?' he says, then turns to Trimble. 'You didn't shoot him did you?' Trimble replies, 'Me... I love dogs... Ask him?'
related_events: Berlin questions Trimble about shooting the dog

name: Berlin and Ross Observe the Bum's Autopsy
description: ROSS holds a Vic inhaler to his nostril as a sharp stench hits, forcing his head back. In the autopsy room, the PATHOLOGIST speaks into a microphone, detailing the examination. He notes the liver shows severe cirrhosis, worse than he's ever seen, and says the man would have died from alcohol even if the knife hadn't killed him. ROSS listens, skeptical. BERLIN asks if the fatal cut was left to right, pointing out the Bum was left-handed. He lifts the nicotine-stained left hand. At the same time, a LAB TECHNICIAN holds out a clipboard, waiting for BERLIN to sign before releasing a picnic box. The PATHOLOGIST shrugs, suggesting the man was too drunk to know which hand he was using. BERLIN returns the clipboard and turns to ROSS, recalling a question from a newspaper reporter at the station: whether the hand was frozen. ROSS has no answer. The PATHOLOGIST continues, stating the liver weighs 1420 grams. He looks at the scale, where a needle trembles, then adds that a few beers wouldn't cause that kind of damage.
related_events: Ross uses Vic inhaler as inadequate defense against sudden stink
Pathologist narrates autopsy findings on the Bum's liver
Berlin examines Bum's left hand and questions handedness of fatal cut
Lab Technician requests Berlin's signature in exchange for picnic box
Pathologist states liver weight and questions alcohol impact

name: Berlin Asks Ross About Reporter's Question on the Frozen Hand
description: After the pathologist finishes speaking about the liver and the cause of death, Berlin steps back from the body. A lab technician approaches him with a clipboard, waiting for a signature in exchange for the picnic box. Berlin signs and turns to Ross, remembering something. He asks Ross why a newspaper reporter at the station would want to know if the victim's hand was frozen. Ross looks up, puzzled, and replies that he has no idea. Berlin chews his gum, the question hanging in the air as the pathologist continues dictating notes and the weighing needle trembles beneath the liver.
related_events: Berlin recalls and questions Ross about newspaper inquiry on frozen hand

name: Berlin and Helena Observe the Return
description: Berlin stands on the fire escape, watching cars arrive and doors slam as students return from the weekend. Voices rise from below, filling the space with a busyness that hasn't been there before. He steps back into the room, where Helena waits. She tells him she went outside to feel the snow on her face, and mentions hearing someone call him John. The two exchange glances, the silence between them thickening. Berlin says it’s not snowing anymore, just getting dark. He looks at her intently, his gaze fixed on her face. After a pause, he asks if she would recognize him again if he were in the room with her. She replies that he’s already asked that. The quiet stretches. Then he says, 'Amber's dead, isn't she?' Helena looks at him. 'Yes,' he says. 'I'm sorry.'
related_events: Berlin observes students returning from the weekend
Berlin and Helena prepare to leave together

name: Helena Recalls Hearing Berlin Called John
description: Helena stands inside the room, explaining she had gone outside to feel the snow on her face. She pauses, then says she thinks that’s when she heard someone call Berlin ‘John.’ Berlin looks at her, his eyes searching her face. The sound of students returning fills the air, but between them, the silence grows. Berlin confirms Amber is dead. He says he’s sorry.
related_events: Helena explains her reason for being outside
Helena recalls hearing someone call him John

name: Berlin Tells Helena That Amber Is Dead
description: Berlin and Helena stand in silence, the air between them heavy. Cars arrive outside, doors slam, and the voices of students echo as they return from the weekend. Berlin has been watching Helena from the fire escape, then reenters the room. She says she went outside to feel the snow on her face, though it is no longer snowing. The light fades as Berlin studies her, his gaze fixed. He asks if she would recognize him again, if he were in the room with her. She replies that he’s already asked that. After a long pause, he says, "Amber's dead, isn't she?" Berlin answers, "Yes. I'm sorry."
related_events: Berlin confirms Amber's death

name: Berlin restores a severed finger for fingerprinting
description: The atrophied hand floats in a container of fluid, its index and middle fingers bound with wire just below the upper joint. Berlin picks up a pair of steel pliers and leans in close. There's a sharp snap as he cuts through one of the fingers, severing it. He sets the finger aside and draws fluid from the container into a syringe. Ross enters, holding a newspaper with a small article and photo of Berlin. "Jesus, you still here?" he asks. Berlin doesn't look up. "What time is it?" Ross checks his watch. "Seven thirty-five. Here, 'Town Gets Top Cop.' I was gonna pin it to your wall." Berlin ignores the paper, picks up the severed finger, and carefully inserts the needle beneath the wire. He presses the plunger slowly, injecting fluid into the pad. The tissue swells slightly under the skin, gradually regaining shape.
related_events: Berlin cuts off a finger from the atrophied hand
Berlin prepares a syringe with fluid from the container
Berlin injects fluid into the finger pad using a syringe

name: Berlin Questions Ross About the 'Frozen' Case
description: Berlin stands over a preserved hand submerged in fluid, the index and second fingers bound with wire just below the upper joint. He picks up a pair of steel pliers. The camera holds on his face as there's a sharp snap—he cuts off one of the fingers. Carefully, he fills a syringe with the same fluid and inserts the needle beneath the wire on the severed finger, injecting it slowly until the pad swells. Ross walks in, holding a newspaper. "Jesus, you still here?" Berlin doesn't look up. "What time is it?" "Seven thirty-five. Here, 'Town Gets Top Cop.' I was gonna pin it to your wall." He holds out the paper, which features a small article and photo of Berlin. Berlin continues working. "Why so coy about the word 'frozen'?" Ross hesitates. "Because, don't get into it." "There's nothing in the files?" Ross watches him closely. "Watch my lips. Don't get into it. Wasn't our case, wasn't our county, and got nothing to do with that."
related_events: Ross enters the room and confronts Berlin
Ross presents a newspaper article about Berlin
Berlin questions Ross about the term "frozen"
Ross refuses to discuss the matter further

name: Ross Demands Fifty Dollars from Berlin
description: Ross walks beside Berlin down the corridor, miming silent ridicule and counting imaginary winnings. He mouths the words 'F.I.F.T.Y' without speaking. Helena passes by, unaware of the exchange. Berlin presses the elevator button, refusing to look at Ross. As the elevator arrives, its voice announces, 'YOU ARE NOW ON THE FOURTH FLOOR.' The doors slide open. Just before they enter, Ross leans in and whispers, 'Fifty fucken dollars, O.K.' Berlin steps into the elevator without responding. As the doors close, a myopic man in thick glasses—lenses like halves of a glass ball—exits and turns to stare back at them.
related_events: Ross baits Berlin with imaginary winnings while walking down the corridor
Berlin calls the elevator and refuses to acknowledge Ross's behavior
Ross demands immediate payment of fifty dollars from Berlin
Ross whispers 'Fifty fucken dollars, O.K.' into Berlin's ear

name: Berlin Asks Helena to Relay a Message
description: Berlin walks down the corridor with Helena, keeping his voice low. He tells her that if the person writes, calls, or makes any kind of contact, she should let him know. He turns toward the elevator, ignoring Ross, who mimics counting money and mouths the word 'Fifty' silently. As the elevator arrives, a voice announces the fourth floor. A man in thick, round glasses steps out, his gaze lingering on them before they enter. Berlin leans close to Helena’s ear and whispers, 'Fifty fucken dollars, O.K.' She tells him she teaches music composition and cello. Ross repeats, 'Fifty of em. And I want em now,' as the doors slide shut.
related_events: Berlin requests Helena to inform him if she receives contact from someone
Helena reveals her profession as a music composition and cello instructor

name: The Myopic Man in the Elevator
description: The elevator reaches the fourth floor with a recorded announcement: 'YOU ARE NOW ON THE FOURTH FLOOR.' The doors slide open, and a man in his early thirties steps out. He wears thick glasses with lenses that resemble halves of a glass ball. Ross and Berlin enter as he exits, both glancing at him. The man pauses and turns back, fixing his gaze on them just as the elevator doors begin to close. They watch him through the narrowing gap, returning his stare.
related_events: Elevator arrives on the fourth floor with automated voice announcement
Myopic man exits elevator and is observed by Ross and Berlin
Myopic man turns to stare at Ross and Berlin after elevator doors begin closing

name: Berlin Takes Close-Up Photographs and Processes Film
description: Berlin captures extreme close-up images with a camera, the flash firing sharply to illuminate fine details like a fingertip. After the shot, he pulls a wad of chewing gum from the side of the camera and puts it back into his mouth. He then activates the automatic rewind function. The mechanical whirring fills the silence as the film spools inside the camera.
related_events: Camera flash fires during close-up photography
Berlin removes chewing gum from camera and returns it to his mouth
Berlin activates automatic rewind on camera

name: Berlin Adds Photos and Makes a Call
description: Berlin moves away from the camera, pulling a wad of chewing gum from its side and returning it to his mouth. The automatic rewind engages, spooling the film in silence. Around him, a clutter of equipment and technical gear litters the space. He walks toward a phone, his eyes fixed on a bulletin board crowded with photographs—each one pinned in sequence, marking hours spent at the dump. A dozen images trace the progression of discoveries, including a bra. Still watching the board, he dials a number. The line clicks and a recorded voice answers: 'This is Mike Blattis. I can't take your call right now. If you have a message, you know the sound.'
related_events: Bulletin board accumulates photographs documenting time at dump
Berlin walks toward a phone while observing photographs
Berlin dials a phone number while studying pictures

name: Berlin Leaves a Message for Mike Blattis
description: Berlin dials Mike Blattis's number, the phone rings, and an automated voicemail greeting begins. A recorded voice informs him that Mike cannot take the call and invites him to leave a message after the tone. Berlin listens without speaking, the line silent except for the prompt. The recording ends, and the call disconnects.

name: Berlin's Morning with Gum and Cigarettes
description: Berlin sits on the mattress, eating a breakfast of chewing gum and milk. He unwraps another piece of Juicy Fruit and chews it, the flavor turning flat and unpleasant in his mouth. Walking into the kitchen, he spits the gum into the sink. He unloads his leather bag, pulling out various items, including a 9mm Beretta and a pack of cigarettes. He lights one, inhaling deeply, the smoke sharp with nicotine and a quiet sense of guilt.

Berlin lights cigarette and inhales deeply with guilt

name: Berlin Listens to a Familiar Voice on the Scanner
description: Berlin sits on the mattress, chewing gum, when a call comes through on the police scanner for 'David 72 Sam 3.' He stops chewing, recognizing the voice immediately. David 72 reports a 927D at the Springfield Street City Dump but says he won’t respond—he’s already outside Emersons, waiting to be the first horrible face of someone’s day. He tells the dispatcher to send other units to secure the location. Berlin exhales slowly, a faint smile crossing his face as he listens.

Berlin reacts with a knowing smile upon hearing David 72's voice
David 72 reports ongoing incident at Springfield Street City Dump

David 72 requests backup to secure the location

name: Moving the Bed Up the Stairs
description: ROSS and BERLIN wrestle a bed up a narrow staircase, the frame catching against the walls with each step. The space is tight, the angle awkward. BOBBY, a 12-year-old nearby, calls out, 'You gotta go left, Dad.' ROSS grunts, 'I know we gotta go left!' They heave together, gaining another step. MARGIE steps out of the kitchen, apron off and coat on. 'You're all done except the floor,' she says. 'The house is a zoo of furniture. Bullshit piled up everywhere.' BERLIN tells her, 'You're a saint, Margie, thanks.' She turns to BOBBY. 'C'mon, Bobby.' 'Don't forget the wagon, Darlin',' she adds. He grabs it, and they leave through a door that slams behind them, just as the phone begins to ring.
related_events: ROSS and BERLIN struggle to move a bed up the stairs
BOBBY gives navigational advice during the move

name: ROSS Reacts to Low Tip After Moving Job
description: BERLIN and ROSS are at opposite ends of a bed stuck on the stairs. ROSS mutters, "Bastards. I gave 'em a 20 buck tip." As they struggle to maneuver the furniture, ROSS listens to various suggestions from others, including a 12-year-old boy named BOBBY, who calls out, "You gotta go left, Dad." ROSS responds, "I know I gotta go left!" Both men heave the bed forward, gaining another step. MARGIE walks out of the kitchen, removes her apron, and puts on her coat. name: Benny Shares His Story at the AA Meeting
description: Benny stands to speak at the Church of St. Peter in Los Angeles during an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting. The room is filled with people, smoke hanging in the air despite a 'NO SMOKING' sign on the wall. He has a weathered face, eyes slow and heavy, and speaks in a low, steady voice. He tells the group that after his third recovery, his wife made him promise never to bring alcohol into the house again. He kept that promise—technically—by burying a bottle under the lawn, covering it with a piece of turf and sealing it with tin foil. On the surface, he looked sober, wearing swimming shorts and lying in the yard as his wife pruned the roses. Beneath the grass, a straw led to the hidden bottle, and he drank quart after quart of wine. He says drunks often find their own madness funny, and he was no different—sick for half his life until he found sobriety in meetings like this one. He looks around and tells the newcomers not to take that first drink, to take it one day at a time, and to keep coming back. The chair thanks him, and the room settles, waiting for the next speaker.
